description: Transcript delta reader (JSONL, byte offsets), entry parsing, offset state files, and assistant-text extraction (v2 caps). Test data only. `expect` holds what the tests assert (keys like "entries_len", "entries[0].text", "[0].length" are paths into the result); `computed_result` is the full Python output. String values may be generator specs ({"$concat": [...]}, {"$repeat": s, "count": n}).
file_notes: Each fixture .jsonl here has LF line ends and the same JSON text the tests wrote (json.dumps default separators). The tests wrote files in text mode, which on Windows produced CRLF; offsets in computed results are for these LF files. Paths in steps are relative to fixtures/capture/; read_transcript_delta needs an absolute path, so join with the absolute fixture dir.

steps: Validate path: "", contains "..", or not absolute -> ([], 0).
Seek to last_offset in binary mode; read line by line (split after b"\n"; the last line may lack it).
Skip a line if len(raw line incl. newline) > MAX_LINE_BYTES (1048576).
Skip if the line is empty after bytes.strip() (ASCII whitespace incl. \x0b and \x0c).
Skip unless the raw bytes contain b'"assistant"' (the 11-byte quoted word).
Skip if not valid UTF-8, not valid JSON, or not a JSON object.
new_offset = position after the last line read = file size at read time (always EOF, even when the last line was skipped or incomplete). OSError during read -> ([], last_offset).
parse_entry: message must be an object; message.content must be an array.
Collect blocks that are objects with type == "text" and a string text whose strip() is non-empty; keep text.strip().
Entry: role "assistant", text, timestamp = str(data.get("timestamp", "")), uuid = str(data.get("uuid", "")), entry_type = "assistant".
reader_rules.docstring_mismatch: The docstring says new_offset is 'the byte position after the last successfully parsed line'; the code returns f.tell() after the loop, i.e. EOF.

state_rules.save: Sanitise session_id (invalid -> no-op). mkdir -p state dir. Write json.dumps({"last_offset": offset, "last_timestamp": timestamp}, ensure_ascii=False) (default separators, no trailing newline) to {session_id}.tmp, then os.replace to {session_id}.json.
state_rules.load: Sanitise session_id (invalid -> defaults). Read and parse; return {last_offset: int(value or 0), last_timestamp: str(value or "")}. FileNotFoundError, JSONDecodeError, ValueError, OSError -> {"last_offset": 0, "last_timestamp": ""}.

steps: For each entry in order: skip unless role == "assistant"; text = entry.text.strip() (Python str.strip, Unicode whitespace); skip if empty.
If total + len(text) > cap: remaining = cap - total; if remaining > 0 append text[:remaining] + "..."; STOP.
extractor_rules_v2.ellipsis: Three ASCII dots "...", appended after the cut; the suffix is not counted toward the cap.

extractor_rules_master.difference: Master cut each entry to 5000 chars and the combined list to 10000 chars, with NO "..." suffix. v2 uses one 200000 cap at both stages and appends "..." when cutting. v2 wins.

reader_cases.name: reads_from_offset
reader_cases.notes: Step 2 passes last_offset = step 0's new_offset and must return no entries and the same offset.

reader_cases.name: reads_appended_entries
reader_cases.notes: The test appends one line to the same file between reads. Here the file before the append is .before.jsonl and after the append is .after.jsonl (the .after file starts with the exact bytes of .before). Run step 0 on .before, then step 1 on .after with step 0's offset.

reader_cases.name: offset_beyond_file_size_resets
reader_cases.notes: last_offset > file size resets to 0 and reads from the start.

reader_cases.name: nonexistent_file
reader_cases.notes: Literal path, not a fixture file. Returns ([], 0) whether the path is rejected by validate_transcript_path (Windows: no drive, not absolute) or does not exist (POSIX).

reader_cases.name: oversized_line_skipped
reader_cases.file_spec_encoding: utf-8, write bytes exactly (LF line ends)
reader_cases.notes: First line is 1,048,689 bytes including its newline (> MAX_LINE_BYTES 1,048,576) and is skipped before any parsing. The file is described by file_spec instead of a 1 MB fixture; materialise it in a temp dir. The oversized check uses the raw line length INCLUDING the trailing newline.

reader_probes.name: no_trailing_newline
reader_probes.notes: Last line has no newline. It is still read and parsed, and new_offset is the file size. A half-written last line that fails to parse is also consumed (offset moves past it).

reader_probes.name: partial_last_line_consumed
reader_probes.notes: Truncated last line (invalid JSON) is skipped AND the offset still moves to EOF, so it will not be re-read on the next call.

reader_probes.name: crlf_line_endings
reader_probes.notes: CRLF files parse the same (json.loads ignores the trailing \r); offsets count the \r bytes.

reader_probes.name: invalid_utf8_line_skipped
reader_probes.notes: A line that is not valid UTF-8 is skipped silently.

reader_probes.name: marker_in_user_text
reader_probes.notes: The bytes pre-filter only checks for the 11 bytes "assistant" (with quotes); a user line containing them is parsed and then rejected by type.

reader_probes.name: multi_text_blocks_joined
reader_probes.notes: Each text block is stripped; blank blocks are dropped; the rest are joined with "\n\n". Missing timestamp/uuid become "".

reader_probes.name: offset_mid_line
reader_probes.notes: An offset that lands mid-line is used as is: the rest of that line is read as a line (invalid JSON here, skipped).

content.text: The fix was to reset the cache.

parse_entry_probes.name: sidechain_truthy_string
parse_entry_probes.notes: isSidechain uses Python truthiness: any non-empty string, non-zero number, non-empty list/object counts as true.

parse_entry_probes.name: sidechain_zero
parse_entry_probes.notes: 0 is falsy, so the entry is kept.

parse_entry_probes.name: timestamp_number
parse_entry_probes.notes: Non-string timestamp/uuid are converted with Python str(): 12 -> '12', null -> 'None'.

state_probes.name: string_offset
state_probes.notes: int() accepts the string '42'; str() turns 7 into '7'.

state_probes.name: array_document
state_probes.notes: A JSON array raises AttributeError on .get, which is NOT caught by load_state (it catches FileNotFoundError, JSONDecodeError, ValueError, OSError only).

state_probes.name: unsafe_session_id
state_probes.notes: session_id is sanitised first (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, <= 128 chars, not a Windows device name); invalid ids load defaults and save nothing.

extractor_cases.name: 250k_combined_truncated
extractor_cases.notes: Computed: first entry intact (125000), second cut to the remaining 75000 chars + '...'. Iteration stops after a truncated entry.

extractor_probes.name: exactly_cap_total
extractor_probes.notes: Total exactly 200000 is allowed (check is total + len > cap). The next entry has remaining == 0, so nothing is appended and iteration stops (no '...').

extractor_probes.name: cap_plus_one_total
extractor_probes.notes: The entry that crosses the cap is cut to the remaining chars + '...'.

extractor_probes.name: truncated_entry_stops_iteration
extractor_probes.notes: After a truncated entry nothing more is returned.

extractor_superseded_by_v2.name: master_combined_budget_enforced
extractor_superseded_by_v2.notes: entry_size = MAX_COMBINED_TEXT // 3 + 100 = 3433. Master truncates without any suffix.
